thread:
incident-bot: PAGING — Routing SLO breach detected in us-west-2. p95=1.1s (SLO 0.8s), p99=4.8s (SLO 3s). Spike started ~5m ago. Error budget alert fired. Streaming stalls observed for a subset of long-lived connections. :rotating_light:

olivia (oncall): I'm on it — creating bridge. Live bridge: https://meet.redwood/bridge/1778009999 

olivia (oncall): initial blamestack looks like a routing policy rollout (weight seeding) that started 12:10UTC. kevin, can you confirm which policy changed?

kevin (router): I rolled out policy 'prefer-local-shards-v2' to 10% at 12:08UTC. rollout job id=rb-v2-2026-03-15-03. Live trace shows ~8% of requests now hitting shard-41 which is on old hw (cpu-heavy) and frequently queues KV cache updates.

samir (eng-sre): seeing strong correlation: traffic histogram shows a tiny fraction of keys hitting shard-41 but those requests have 99th ~9.2s and are causing backpressure into the streaming mux. Logs: `router: routing_decision shard=41 weight=0.08 backend_cpu=32% kv-cache-miss-rate=0.42`

maya (support): we got three customer reports of streaming stalls (chat messages delayed) — accounts: acme-inc, bluebox, neatdocs. All in us-west-2. No SLA escalations yet but customers are noticing.

olivia (oncall): severity = Sev2 -> escalate to oncall-bridge. Prioritize rollbacks or emergency override. We want minimal blast radius. Plan: 1) pause rollout, 2) activate regional-affinity-override to avoid shard-41, 3) drain shard-41 slowly. Thoughts?

kevin (router): I can pause rollout immediately: `kubectl patch rollout rb-v2-... --patch '{"spec":{"paused":true}}'` — done. Paused at ~10%.

ops-bot: rollout rb-v2-2026-03-15-03 paused by kevin at 12:20UTC.

samir (eng-sre): pushing an override now: `curl -XPOST https://router-admin/api/v1/override -d '{"region":"us-west-2","avoid_shard":41,"reason":"live mitigation"}'` — override accepted, routing weight for shard-41 set to 0.0 for 10m.

incident-bot: Override applied: avoid_shard=41 TTL=600s by samir. Telemetry will reflect change within ~1 min.

kevin (router): traffic is shifting off shard-41, p99 falling from 4.8s -> 2.9s within 90s. Streaming stall count dropping.

maya (support): still seeing a trickle of customer impact (delays ~2-3s), but fewer stalls. I'll update ACME and Bluebox with mitigation notes.

samir (eng-sre): root cause hypothesis: weight seeding algorithm computed weights using a stale zone-capacity vector. Seed produced a hot weight for shard-41; because shard-41 holds some long-lived streaming state, it makes tails worse. We'll need a fix to the seed generator to prefer per-shard queue-depth metrics.

olivia (oncall): agree. For live mitigation we did: pause rollout, override avoid_shard, and enabled a temporary eager-fallback policy so requests hitting degraded backends fall back to lower-latency variant. I triggered `policy:eager-fallback=true` in us-west-2.

kevin (router): enabled eager-fallback. Counter-intuitive note: fallback increases overall token-cost but drops tail latency instantly for streaming. p99 now ~1.8s.

ops-bot: policy change recorded: eager-fallback=true in us-west-2 by olivia. Audit-id=AU-177800-3

samir (eng-sre): telemetry snapshot attached in bridge. Key numbers: pre-mitigation p99=4.8s, post-override p99=1.8s, streaming stall rate down 87%. No crash loops on router.

maya (support): customers updated. ACME is impacted but not on bankruptcy watch :slightly_smiling_face:. They're okay with rollback plan.

olivia (oncall): Next steps: 1) keep override for 15m, 2) start safe drain of shard-41 -> migrate streaming sessions to warm replicas, 3) create rollback PR for seeding algorithm, 4) do a controlled canary of rb-v2 once seed fix is in, 5) prepare postmortem. Assign owners: samir -> drain and telemetry, kevin -> seed fix PR, maya -> customer comms.

samir (eng-sre): Taking drain. Command to migrate sessions: `scripts/migrate_streams --from-shard 41 --to-pool usw2-warm --concurrency 20`. Starting migration now. Progress: 0/248 sessions -> 180/248 in 6m. No new stalls.

kevin (router): I'll open PR: "seed: prefer-queue-depth-over-static-capacity" — linking shortly. Should include regression test that simulates long-lived streaming keys.

olivia (oncall): couple of action items for postmortem: - why seed used stale vector - why health signal for streaming queue depth not in seeding pipeline - improve alerting to include streaming-stall metric with p95/p99 per-shard.

ops-bot: Migration job 1778009999 started by samir. job_id=mig-177800-1

samir (eng-sre): migration complete. 248/248 sessions moved, shard-41 traffic ~0.6%. p99 stabilized to 0.9s.

maya (support): informed customers. ACME: "thanks — latency improved, will monitor". Bluebox: "saw it, ok now". No open cases.

olivia (oncall): handing off to samir for post-incident work. I'm signing off from bridge. Samir, please include timeline and customer impact in the postmortem.

samir (eng-sre): taking over. Notes: incident start 12:10UTC, mitigation applied 12:20UTC (override), migration done 12:36UTC. Total customer-facing impact ~26m for a tiny subset of streaming customers. Next: ship seed fix, add e2e test, add alert rule for streaming-stall-rate > 3/min.

maya (support): I'll attach the customer comms thread and copy of messages.

kevin (router): PR opened: https://git.redwood/repo/pulls/4123 — seed fix included. Requesting reviews from eng-ml + eng-runtime.

samir (eng-sre): closing bridge. leaving this thread for handoff notes. If anything regresses ping me.

incident-bot: Incident closed to oncall at 12:45UTC by samir. Final p99 in us-west-2: 0.9s.

olivia (oncall): thanks team. Logged Sev2 and assigned postmortem owner samir.

samir (eng-sre): Postmortem checklist created: https://docs.redwood/pm/1778009999. Will add TL;DR and customer impact section tonight.

maya (support): adding support notes and customer snippets to the doc.

kevin (router): follow-up: schedule a canary of rb-v2 only after we have queue-depth telemetry integrated into seeding.

samir (eng-sre): acknowledged. Closing thread.
